story: When you look up at the Moon, it feels like our cozy neighbor in space. But that impression is completely misleading. The gap separating the Earth and the Moon is so vast that every single other planet in our solar system can fit inside it side by side, with room to spare. The Moon sits at an average distance of about 384,400 kilometers from Earth. If you line up Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune by their diameters, their combined widths total just under 400,000 kilometers. Even though gas giants like Jupiter and Saturn dwarf everything else, they still comfortably squeeze into the available space when the Moon reaches the farthest part of its elliptical orbit at apogee.
angle: Every other planet in the solar system can fit in the gap between the Earth and the Moon with room to spare.

claims.claim: The Moon sits at an average distance of about 384,400 kilometers from Earth.
The Moon follows an elliptical path rather than a perfectly circular one, changing its distance from Earth.
The Moon is moving away from the Earth at an average rate of 3.8 cm per year.
Light takes about 1.3 seconds to travel from the Moon back to the Earth.
The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite.
The Moon has an average distance of about 238,855 to 238,860 miles from Earth.
